sections.h2: What does the Scotland County Register of Deeds do?
sections.html:
The Scotland County Register of Deeds is the custodian of deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney, plats and other legal papers for the county, and it also issues vital records and records military discharges. If you sell a house in Scotland County, the deed that moves title to your buyer ends up in this office.

The county site separates its land records into several tools. Documents from 1978 to the present and all plats sit in one index that you open by signing in as a guest. Older documents have their own pre-1978 search. The county also links its GIS map and a listing of tax foreclosures.

For rights of way from before 1978, the office asks you to email it the book and page references. Bring those references if you are tracing an old easement across a Scotland County lot.

sections.h2: How can I look up a Scotland County property record before I sell?
sections.html:
Start with the online index, then use the GIS map if you do not have the owner's name. The county's records page explains that the Laurinburg and Scotland County GIS often gives the owner's name and, in most cases, a book and page reference to the deed.

  • Use the 1978 to present index for recent deeds, deeds of trust and plats.
  • Use the pre-1978 search for older instruments in the chain of title.
  • Open the tax foreclosure listing if you suspect a parcel has a tax case against it.
  • Set up PropertyCheck, which sends an alert when a filing appears under a name you monitor.

Pulling your own deed and any open deed of trust before you list gives you a picture of what a buyer's title company will find. A lien you did not know about is easier to clear while no contract is pending.

sections.h2: What must be true before Scotland County will accept a deed?
sections.html:
The office reviews each instrument against statutory prerequisites, and the county posts the common ones. The state's Document Standards must be followed as well.

  • The paper must generally be the original, with original signatures and proof of acknowledgement or notarization.
  • A deed or deed of trust drawn in North Carolina must carry the name of the person or law firm that drafted it on the first page.
  • Recording fees must be paid before the instrument is filed, unless a statute allows recording without charge.
  • A conveyance of real property, other than a deed of trust or mortgage, must show the excise tax the grantor owes.

The office states that it may not give legal advice or help prepare documents. Questions about how to word a deed belong with an attorney.

sections.h2: Do delinquent taxes block a Scotland County deed?
sections.html:
They can. The county says that since July 1, 2020, a deed transferring real property is not accepted unless the Scotland County tax collector has certified that no delinquent county, municipal or other collector-charged taxes are a lien on the property.

There is a second route. The deed may instead carry a statement that a licensed North Carolina attorney prepared it and that any delinquent taxes will be paid to the county tax collector by the closing attorney when closing proceeds are disbursed. This is why many Scotland County closings run through an attorney's trust account.

State law explains why the collector's certificate matters. The lien for property tax attaches as of the listing date (G.S. 105-355), and a tax foreclosure ends with a courthouse door auction that can wipe out most other liens (G.S. 105-374). Ask the tax collector for a payoff figure early.

sections.h2: What does recording cost in Scotland County?
sections.html:
Fees are fixed statewide, and the table shows the main ones with the excise tax rate printed on the Scotland County page.

Recording fees and excise tax relevant to a Scotland County sale
ItemPrinted figureSource
Instrument in general$26.00 for the first 15 pages, plus $4.00 for each added pageG.S. 161-10
Mortgage or deed of trust$64.00 for the first 35 pages, plus $4.00 for each added pageG.S. 161-10
Satisfaction or cancellationNo feeG.S. 161-10
Plat$21.00 per sheetG.S. 161-10
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each added pageG.S. 161-10
Excise tax on a deed$2 per $1000, paid by the grantorScotland County page

The $2 per $1000 figure on the county page is the same rate the statute states as $1.00 for each $500 (G.S. 105-228.30). The county page lists exempt transfers: by gift, by intestacy, by lease for a term of years, by merger or consolidation, by operation of law, and under a will.

sections.h2: Why does the order of recording matter in Scotland County?
sections.html:
A deed, or a lease of more than three years, is good against lien creditors and buyers for value only from the time it is registered in the county where the land lies, and priority follows the order of registration (G.S. 47-18).

For a seller, this means the deed to your buyer and the buyer's lender's deed of trust should be filed together and promptly. It also means your own payoff and satisfaction should be recorded so the old loan stops showing against the parcel. Recording a satisfaction costs nothing under G.S. 161-10.

A late filing is simply later in line. Ask your closing attorney for the recording time of each instrument, and keep a copy of the recorded deed with its book and page numbers for your own files and for any future title question. If a number looks wrong, ask the office to correct the index.

sections.h2: How should heirs or owners with unusual situations approach Scotland County recording?
sections.html:
The register of deeds records what it is handed, and the paper work upstream usually happens elsewhere. These are the common cases:

  • Heirs of a small estate may use a clerk of court affidavit under G.S. 28A-25-1 when personal property, less liens, is $20,000 or less, after waiting 30 days from death.
  • An owner who sells on a payment plan under a contract for deed must record the contract or a memorandum of it within five business days (Chapter 47H).
  • A foreclosure bidder may be outbid: an upset bid must top the last bid by 5 percent, with a minimum increase of $750, within ten days (G.S. 45-21.27).

Once the court or attorney completes those steps, the resulting deed is recorded under the same rules above.

faqs.q: Can I search Scotland County deeds online?
faqs.a: Yes. The county site offers an index for 1978 to the present plus all plats, entered by signing in as a guest, and a separate search for pre-1978 documents. A GIS map helps when you do not know the owner's name.

faqs.q: What is the excise tax rate on a deed in Scotland County?
faqs.a: The county page prints $2 per $1000, paid by the grantor. That matches the state statute rate of $1.00 per $500. Gifts, transfers by intestacy and transfers under a will are among the listed exceptions.

faqs.q: Does Scotland County require proof of paid taxes to record a deed?
faqs.a: Yes. Since July 1, 2020 the county accepts a real property deed only with the tax collector's certificate of no delinquent taxes, or with an attorney's statement that delinquent taxes will be paid from closing proceeds.

faqs.q: Does the Scotland County office help me write a deed?
faqs.a: No. The office says it may not practice law, so it cannot help prepare documents or answer legal questions. Use an attorney, who must also be named on the first page of the deed as its preparer.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to record a satisfaction of a deed of trust in Scotland County?
faqs.a: No. G.S. 161-10 sets no fee for recording satisfactions or cancellations. Make sure your lender files one after you pay off the loan so the lien clears from the index.
